value: The first step in completing the ASU undergraduate application is the My Information section.
The second section of the application focuses on your prior academic history, including high school and any colleges or universities you previously attended.
Students have the option to self-report high school grades in the My Grades section of the application, though self-reporting is not required.
The information shared in the residency portion of the undergraduate application helps determine if you are an in-state, out-of-state, or international student.
If you're unsure about what major is best for you, resources are offered to help you decide, and you can change your major later.
Review your application, submit it, and pay the application fee.

facts.value: Available for first-year students admitted in spring 2026 or earlier, up to a maximum of eight semesters, beginning with their first term of enrollment at ASU.
Available for two-year community college transfer students admitted in spring 2026 or earlier, up to a maximum of 5 semesters, beginning with their first term of enrollment at ASU.
Available for four-year institution transfer students admitted in spring 2026 or earlier, up to a maximum of 120 credit hours, including all transfer credits.
Students must maintain continuous enrollment which is defined as enrollment in both fall and spring semesters with summer sessions not included.
Students must earn a minimum of 24 credits during the yearly fall/spring review period.
Students may not use summer sessions and consortium agreement classes, repeated classes, incomplete grades or audited classes to meet the minimum 24 credit hours requirement.
Any credits received by examination, including AP, CLEP, IB and other tests, do not count towards the minimum 24 credit hours requirement.
Students must maintain a 2.00 minimum ASU cumulative GPA.
Students are expected to enroll in classes at their designated campus location. Courses delivered through iCourse are allowed.
